contract.words: Collect $1,500 of settled cash within 21 days with no more than 4 hours a week of owner time.

terms.proofCondition: $1,500 of settled cash received in the owner's account within 21 days

strategy.title: No plan: the only opening needs far more owner hours than 4 a week allows
strategy.why: Same-week service of process is fulfilled by the owner personally at 3 hours per serve. Reaching $1,500 settled needs 19 serves at $95 less $12 direct cost ($1,577 net), i.e. 57 owner hours; the goal allows 4 hours a week x 3 weeks = 12 hours, enough for 4 serves ($332 net). The 20 recorded agreements would need 60 owner hours. No other fulfiller is named on the card.

alternatives.title: Serve only what 12 owner hours allow
Subcontract the serves to another process server
alternatives.why: No subcontractor, its price or availability is on the record; the card names the owner as the fulfiller.

The county's three largest process-serving firms list $95 for standard service completed within 7 days (published rate cards, 2026-10).

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is the right stance and the decisive gap is a true constraint, not missing evidence. The only opening (same-week service of process) has every link established, including 20 written acceptances at $95 ($1,900 gross), but its recorded fulfiller is the owner personally at 3 hours per serve (card fulfillmentOwner + humanHours 3). Recomputed: net per serve $95 - $12 = $83; $1,500 / $83 = 18.07, so 19 serves = 57 owner hours (all 20 agreements = 60 h, matching Brain's figure); the goal allows 4 h/week x 3 weeks = 12 h = 4 serves = $332 net. Even with every agreement in hand the evidence cannot fit the hours limit, which is what a constraint is. Settlement (10 days of 21) and cost are not the binding issue. No other fulfiller is on the record, so treating a subcontractor as available would be an unknown read as favourable; the plan correctly names it as the way out (a server below $83/serve) alongside raising the limit to ~19 h/week. The constraint basis cites the card's humanHours field.
findings: INFO cop_2c630ec307bf4c3499e6 FULFILMENT: owner-personal fulfilment at 3 h/serve x 19 serves = 57 h vs 12 h allowed — binding OWNER_HOURS constraint.
LOW cop_2c630ec307bf4c3499e6 OFFER_AND_PRICE: price fact cites competitors' rate cards, but 20 written acceptances at $95 on the card establish this buyer's price independently.
LOW: the $95 price is also the median competitor list price; a subcontractor quote under $83 is the decisive evidence that would turn this into a plan with ~1-2 owner hours of selling and collecting.
